data.title: Browser Issues: ITP, Cookies, Redirection
data.body:
I added some debug logging.

The `checkSameSiteNoneCompatible()` method in `CookieHelper.php` is returning `true`.

The redirect back to login happens in `AuthController.php` because `$status` is null returning from `AuthenticateShop::__invoke()` because the call to `$this->apiHelper->verifyRequest` is returning false.

The `Request` object seems valid in that it has a shop, a timestamp and an hmac (plus a code which doesn't seem to be used in verifyRequest).  However, the params also contain `"q":"/authenticate"` ... removing that from the params (           `unset($params['q']);`) before computing the hmac hash allows it to work correctly and redirect to the shopify store after authentication.

After redirection, I see the app loaded correctly in the shopify admin interface. 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/249841/88070737-0414b480-cb41-11ea-84f1-86a4e8a27fc7.png)

 However, in the Apps list, I still see this after a fresh install of the app.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/249841/88070797-155dc100-cb41-11ea-9195-14333a4796a5.png)

I would recommend changing `verifyRequest` to only include keys from `$params` that should be in the hmac hash calculation, I think that is part of `osiset/BasicShopifyAPI` though.

data.title: Browser Issues: ITP, Cookies, Redirection
data.body:
I've had some success now by probing the Koa implementation.

I believe my flow needs to be this:

- ITP middleware will check for ITP cookie
- If ITP cookie does not exist, redirect to top level and set a same site cookie, then redirect back to app with a query param of ?itp=true
- Once redirected back to app, it'll run through ITP middleware again, we will check for ITP cookie, if it doesn't exist and the ITP query param exists, then we need to redirect to a cookie/storage permission page
- On this page, using JS, user will read a prompt and click to try and enable cookies / storage access
- Some browsers will prompt to confirm, others just allow it
- Once this is done, were good to redirect back and have cookie access


With this plan in mind and loosely working I'll continue to develop a solution.

@faizan-glowlogix and @nguyenduc308 

I've managed to fix this.
Whenever you try to follow a link or click the app bridge button, always pass the 'shop' param into your route.

for example,

Instead of using this:
`{{ route('home') }}`

Use this:
`{{ route('home', ['shop' => auth()->user()->name ]) }}`


I hope it will help you too.
